chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Isṣ, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said:

I said to Abū al-Ḥasan (peace be upon him): 'A man marries a woman in Muṭʿah (temporary marriage). She stipulates to him that she will come to him every day until she fulfills his condition, or she stipulates certain known days during which she will come to him. Then she deceives him and does not come to him as stipulated. Is it permissible for him to hold her accountable for the days she did not come, so that he withholds from her dower based on that calculation?'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes. He looks at what was cut off from the stipulation, so he withholds from her dower by the amount of what she did not fulfill for him, except for the days of menstruation, for they are for her. Thus, there is not for him except what was permissible for him of her private parts.'
ai.seo_question: How is the dower calculated in temporary marriage if the wife misses the agreed-upon days?
ai.summary: In this ruling from al-Kāfī, Imam al-Riḍā (peace be upon him) clarifies the financial accountability in temporary marriage (Muṭʿah), establishing that the husband may deduct from the dower only for the specific days the wife failed to appear, while excluding menstruation as a valid excuse. This hadith underscores the contractual precision of Shia jurisprudence, treating the stipulated days as a quantifiable right of the husband that is forfeited only by mutual agreement or natural impediment, thereby protecting the wife's financial rights during periods of menstruation.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said,

‘I said to Abu Al-Hassanasws, ‘The man marries the woman by Mut’a. She stipulates to him that she would come to him every day until his stipulation is fulfilled, or she stipulates certain known days during which she would come to him. So she betrays him with it and does not come to him upon what had been stipulated upon her. So is it correct for him that he accounts her upon what she did not come to him from the days, so that he would withhold from her dower by the accounting of that?’

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes. He would look at what was cut-off from the stipulation, so he would withhold from her from her dower by a measurement of whatever she did not fulfill for him, except for the days she menstruated in, so it would be for her. Thus, there would not happen to be for him except for what was Permissible for him of her private parts’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following:

“About the case of a man who marries a woman in the manner of al-Mut‘ah (advantageous marriage) with the condition that she must come to him every day to comply with the condition, or sets a condition to come to him in certain days; but she asks to be excused and does not come to comply with the condition; if it is proper for him to deduct for the days that she did not come and withhold from her mahr (dower) accordingly. To this question from me

abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, said, ‘Yes, he can consider how much she has violated, then withhold proportionate to what she has not complied, except the days of her Hayd (menses); they are for her and he cannot have what is not lawful for him in matters of going to bed with her.’”
